title: Registry isolation checks were bypassed through React element factory APIs

examples: import { createElement as h } from 'react'; h('iframe', { sandbox: '', src: '/same-origin' })
reproduction.beforeFix: The registry gate accepted native script/iframe nodes and remote image requests when created through React.createElement or JSX runtime factories rather than JSX syntax.
reproduction.afterFix: The scanner resolves React default/named imports, aliases, and jsx/jsxs/jsxDEV runtime factories, then applies native tag and resource-URL rules to their props. External anchors and local image paths remain allowed.

rootCause: Native element and resource URL checks were driven primarily by JSX AST nodes, while React factory calls encode the same DOM output as ordinary call expressions.
remediation: Recognize React.createElement, imported createElement aliases, and react/jsx-runtime factories; run the same script/iframe/remote-resource checks on static tags and props, preserving safe link navigation and local assets.

validation.redBeforeFix: pnpm exec vitest run packages/registry-gate/src/__tests__/registry-gate.test.ts -t "unsafe native resources passed through React element factories"
validation.redBeforeFixResult: failed as expected: script, iframe, and remote image factory calls passed before the fix
validation.safeNavigationRegression: passed: external anchor URLs remain allowed
validation.safeLocalAssetRegression: passed: local image src values remain allowed

runtimeBoundary: This is static registry source analysis. Factory calls were parsed, not executed. The local source-isolation matrix passes all canonical resources; release-candidate deployment verification remains pending.
